newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly lower on Thursday with talk that the central bank is likely to cut the bank reserve ratios in the short term surfacing again, traders said.
But an official with the central bank told Reuters there was no such plan as of now.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract fell to 4.40 percent from 5.20 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose slightly to 2.03 million lots from 1.69 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the talk prevented some big institutions, including securities houses, from trading actively today.
"The three-day contract fell sharply mainly due to heavy institutional selling," said one trader.
But modest rises on the domestic A share markets gave the contract some support, traders said.
They said they expected the rates to consolidate around current levels on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Thursday and two long-term, high-yield contracts rose amid the talk of a cut in bank reserve ratios, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 112.70 yuan from 112.61 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.59 million lots from 901,336 lots.

Traders said after sharp rises in the past few weeks, the yields of the early-maturing contracts had fallen to around 9.5 percent. Only the two longest contracts still have yields of more than 10 percent.
"The talk of cutting bank reserve ratios supported the two high-yield contracts today," one trader said.
Traders said if the reserve ratio cut proved true, institutions were likely to unwind their positions in these contracts and take profits.
